subtopic_detail: Post UTI imaging decision at 20 months per RCH
stem:
You are the paediatric ward registrar reviewing a 20 month old girl in outpatient clinic 6 weeks after her first culture positive urinary tract infection. She was treated in the community with oral trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole after her general practitioner sent a clean catch urine that grew Escherichia coli sensitive to trimethoprim.

She was systemically well throughout, defervesced within 24 hours of starting antibiotics, and has since been thriving. She had a normal 18 to 20 week antenatal morphology scan reported by her mother, with no antenatal renal tract abnormality documented. She has no family history of vesicoureteric reflux, has never had a febrile UTI before, is fully toilet trained by day, and is passing a good stream on the potty. Growth centiles and blood pressure today are both on the 50th centile for age and sex.

Her examination today is unremarkable and a repeat urine is negative on dipstick and microscopy.

data_table.Vital signs: HR 108/min; BP 92/54 mmHg (50th centile); RR 24/min; SpO2 99% RA; T 36.7 C
data_table.Examination: Well grown, unremarkable abdominal and genital exam
data_table.Investigations: Repeat urine microscopy and culture negative today
data_table.History: First febrile UTI 6 weeks ago; E coli sensitive to trimethoprim; defervesced within 24 h; normal 18 to 20 week morphology scan; no family history of VUR

lead_in: What is the most appropriate imaging plan?

options.text: Reassure and arrange no imaging; advise on prompt culture and treatment of any future febrile urinary tract infection episode and safety net for return
options.rationale: RCH advises no imaging after a single typical febrile UTI in a well thriving child aged 6 months to less than 3 years with normal antenatal monitoring; parents are counselled to seek review with any future febrile illness (Source: RCH CPG Urinary tract infection).

options.text: Arrange a dimercaptosuccinic acid renal scan at 6 months to look for cortical scarring and any evidence of pyelonephritic damage to the kidneys
options.rationale: Dimercaptosuccinic acid scanning is a NICE construct and is not part of the RCH imaging cascade; it should not be requested after a single typical UTI (Source: RCH CPG Urinary tract infection).

options.text: Arrange a micturating cystourethrogram to grade vesicoureteric reflux and guide any decision about continuous low dose antibiotic prophylaxis in this child
options.rationale: Micturating cystourethrogram is invasive, involves radiation and catheterisation, and is not in the RCH cascade after a single typical UTI in a child with normal antenatal imaging (Source: RCH CPG Urinary tract infection).

options.text: Arrange a renal tract ultrasound this week to look at renal size, exclude occult obstruction, and confirm no residual pelvicalyceal dilatation
options.rationale: Ultrasound is only indicated for atypical UTI features, recurrent UTI, or infants under 6 months without antenatal monitoring; a single typical UTI in a well thriving girl with a normal antenatal scan does not need ultrasound (Source: RCH CPG Urinary tract infection).

options.text: Start continuous low dose trimethoprim prophylaxis for 12 months and arrange imaging if any further culture positive UTI occurs during the treatment period
options.rationale: Prophylactic antibiotics are not recommended after a single typical UTI in this age group; the PRIVENT trial and RCH guidance restrict prophylaxis to selected recurrent UTI or dilating reflux (Source: RCH CPG Urinary tract infection).

explanation.summary: The RCH imaging cascade after urinary tract infection reserves renal tract ultrasound for atypical UTI, recurrent UTI, infants under 6 months without antenatal monitoring, or when there is a family history of significant renal tract disease. A single typical UTI in a well thriving child between 6 months and 3 years with a normal antenatal morphology scan needs no imaging. Dimercaptosuccinic acid scanning and micturating cystourethrogram are NICE constructs and are not part of the RCH cascade. Parents are safety netted for prompt review and culture of any future febrile illness.
key_points: Single typical UTI plus normal antenatal scan plus well child equals no imaging.
Ultrasound only for atypical, recurrent, under 6 months, or absent antenatal monitoring.
DMSA and MCUG are not part of the RCH cascade.
explanation.pearls: Confirm the antenatal morphology scan was actually done and normal before deciding not to image; a missed antenatal scan converts a first typical UTI in an infant under 6 months into an indication for renal tract ultrasound.
